origins: In some homes, gifts were the main way love was spoken. A parent who worked long hours may have shown care by providing, buying, and fixing, and may have found it hard to say the words. Or a parent who could not afford much may have felt like a failure. Children can learn that love equals what you give or get, and adults can then measure affection by price tags, or feel unloved when the gifts stop.
teaches: Scripture honors generosity, and giving can truly be a way of loving. But Paul says that even if I give all I possess to the poor, but have not love, I gain nothing. John says let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth. Proverbs says that a dish of vegetables where there is love is better than a fattened ox with hatred. Love often includes gifts, but it is shown most deeply through time, presence, honesty, and faithfulness.
self_statements: If they really loved me, they would buy me this.
I show my kids I love them by giving them things.
Without gifts, I do not know how to show care.
When money is tight, I cannot be a good parent or spouse.
errors: Feeling loved only when gifts arrive and concluding that love is gifts.
Believing love is either expensive or absent.
Assuming that someone’s lack of gifts means they do not care.
Treating a missing gift as proof of missing love.
questions: How did my family show love, and with what?
What else did love look like in my home besides gifts?
What do I wish I had received besides things?
How do I try to show love now, and does it match what people need?
What does it cost people when love is shown only through money?
What is one way I can show love this week that costs nothing?
truth: Gifts can be an expression of love, but they are not the same thing as love. Love is also time, words, presence, and faithfulness. I can receive and give love in ways that do not depend on what money can buy.
hw_truths: Gifts are one expression of love, not the whole of it.
I can say “I love you” in words.
I do not need to buy love.
I am loved even when I have little to give.
God’s love is not measured in things.
log: Each day, write one way you gave or received love that did not cost money.
actions: List five ways love has been shown to you.
Circle the ones that did not involve money.
Spend an hour with someone with no phone and no purchase.
Tell someone close to you, in words, what you appreciate about them.
Ask someone you love, “How do you feel most cared for?” and listen.
prayer: Father, thank You for loving me without a price tag. Heal what I learned about love and things. Teach me to give and receive love through time, truth, and faithfulness. Amen.
hw_questions: How did my family show love?
What did I want besides gifts?
How do I show love now?
What does the person I love need?
What is one free way to show love today?
Where have I measured love by things?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can love in action and truth, with time and words as well as gifts.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Love is shown through things.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
